page: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v7 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, featuring 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs without multithreading overhead (1 thread per core). The processor includes 48 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside vector instruction extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. The instance pairs this compute capacity with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU ratio. It operates without bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded performance driven by the high CPU clock speed. In single-core evaluations, the F4ams_v7 achieved top-tier rankings in stress-ng (3,658.18) and Geekbench (2,447.0), with single-threaded compression and decompression reaching 40.49 GB/sec in gzip and 17.89 GB/sec in bzip3. Text processing in Geekbench also placed in the top tier at 3,221.0 points. In contrast, aggregate multi-threaded metrics such as stress-ng multi-core (14,630.16), Geekbench multi-core (7,577.0), and PassMark CPU (13,311.69) fall within average mid-tier ranges, consistent with the four-core ceiling.

Memory throughput reaches 831.45 GB/sec for small cached reads, while large-block uncached read and write bandwidths measure 53.49 GB/sec and 34.49 GB/sec respectively. Synthetic operational testing shows steady throughput across in-memory and web tasks, recording 12.85 million Redis SET operations per second and 10.67 GB/sec in static web serving. While lightweight LLM text generation with a 135M parameter model reached a top-tier 337.36 tokens/sec, larger 7B models exposed compute limits, yielding 30.54 tokens/sec on prompt ingestion and 10.63 tokens/sec on generation.

With its 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high single-core execution speed, the F4ams_v7 provides strong resource density for workloads constrained by single-thread latency or memory capacity rather than parallel core count. Because it lacks integrated local disks, external storage must be provisioned over the network. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, single-threaded processing queues, medium-scale web application runtimes, and caching layers requiring dedicated CPU allocation.
description: Microsoft Azure F4ams_v7 is an x86_64 instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores (4 vCPUs) from an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of RAM. Configured with an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, it incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and cryptographic accelerators, while omitting local storage and discrete GPUs. Benchmark results highlight top-tier single-core performance, evidenced by high Geekbench single-core, single-threaded gzip compression, and fast small-model LLM generation. Multi-core compute metrics, Redis throughput (12.85 million ops/sec), and uncached memory bandwidth align within mid-tier performance envelopes due to the 4-core limit. Requiring network-attached storage, this VM is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, caching servers, in-memory databases, and compute tasks dependent on high single-threaded clock frequencies.
